title: DNA Structure
page_title: DNA Structure | Cambridge (CIE) IGCSE Biology Revision Notes 2021

blocks.name: Structure of a DNA molecule: Extended
blocks.definition:
Describe the structure of a DNA molecule:
(a) two strands coiled together to form a double
helix
(b) each strand contains chemicals called bases
(c) bonds between pairs of bases hold the strands together
(d) the bases always pair up in the same way: A with T, and C with G (full names are not required)

blocks.text: Structure of a DNA molecule: Extended

blocks.md:
- DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the molecule that contains the instructions for the growth and development of all organisms
- It consists of two strands of DNA wound around each other in what is called a **double helix**

blocks.alt: Diagram showing DNA double helix forming a DNA strand, packed into a chromosome (with further detail in a label that a chromosome is a long strand of DNA wrapped around proteins) inside the nucleus of a cell with other organelles present (mitochondria, cytoplasm and cell membrane)
blocks.caption: DNA, chromosomes and the nucleus

blocks.md: - The individual units of DNA are called **nucleotides**

blocks.alt: Diagram of a DNA nucleotide labelled with a phosphate group and deoxyribose sugar which forms the DNA strand backbone, and an attached nitrogenous base A in this image (with a label that the nitrogenous base could be A, T, C or G)
blocks.caption: A nucleotide

blocks.md:
- All nucleotides contain the same phosphate and deoxyribose sugar, but differ from each other in the **base** attached
- There are four different bases, **Adenine (A), Cytosine (C), Thymine (T) and Guanine (G)**
- The bases on each strand pair up with each other, holding the two strands of DNA in the double helix
- The bases always pair up in the same way:

  - Adenine always pairs with Thymine **(A-T)**
  - Cytosine always pairs with Guanine **(C-G)**

blocks.alt: Diagram of DNA double helix showing coloured base pairs A–T and C–G joined by hydrogen bonds, and a labelled sugar–phosphate backbone on the outer edge of each strand
blocks.caption: DNA base pairs

blocks.md: - The phosphate and sugar section of the nucleotides form the ‘backbone’ of the DNA strand (like the sides of a ladder) and the base pairs of each strand connect to form the rungs of the ladder

blocks.alt: Diagram of DNA showing on the left an unwound DNA double helix, illustrating a sequence of base pairs (with A always paired with T and C paired with G) on two antiparallel strands, and the image on the right shows a double helix, there is a note that genes are sequences of bases, not base pairs
blocks.caption: The DNA helix is made from two strands of DNA held together by hydrogen bonds

blocks.md: - It is this sequence of bases that holds the code for the formation of proteins

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: You do not need to learn the names of the bases, **just their letter**. Make sure you **know which bonds with which**, as this is the most commonly asked question about this topic.
